title: Reality of exterior powers
statement:
If $\mathcal G_0$ is an $\iota$-real lisse Weil sheaf, then
$\bigwedge^r\mathcal G_0$ (the exterior power of
[def-real-weil-representation-operations]) is $\iota$-real for every
$0\le r\le\rank(\mathcal G_0)$.

proof.text: As in [p-real-operations], the lisse Weil sheaves here are those on the curve $C_0$ of [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence], and the exterior power of [def-real-weil-representation-operations] is applied to them through that exact tensor equivalence: if $\mathcal G_0$ corresponds to the Weil representation $(V,\rho)$, then $\bigwedge^r\mathcal G_0$ is the lisse Weil sheaf corresponding to $\bigwedge^rV$, on which $g\in W(C_0)$ acts by $\bigwedge^r\rho(g)$, sending $v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_r$ to $\rho(g)v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\rho(g)v_r$; for $r=0$ this is $\Qlb$ with trivial action. Fix a closed point $x$, a geometric Frobenius element $F_x\in W(C_0)$ at $x$, and put $f=\rho(F_x)\in\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Applying [p-real-operations] to $\mathcal G_0$ and to $\bigwedge^r\mathcal G_0$ gives, for the local characteristic factors of [def-wf-iota-real], $P_x(\mathcal G_0,T)=\det(1-Tf\mid V)$ and $P_x(\bigwedge^r\mathcal G_0,T)=\det(1-T\bigwedge^rf\mid\bigwedge^rV)$.

source.place: opening sentence: Frobenius on the exterior-power stalk, through the chapter's representation correspondence

proof.text: Let $s=\dim V$ and enumerate the eigenvalues of $f$, after applying $\iota$, as $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s$, with repetitions. The coefficient field is algebraically closed and $V$ is finite dimensional. Apply the exterior-power clause of [p-linear-spectra] to $f$ and use that $\iota$ preserves finite products. The complex eigenvalue multiset of $\bigwedge^r f$ is therefore $M_r=\{\prod_{i\in I}\lambda_i: I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\},\ |I|=r\}$, with one occurrence for each indexed subset. No diagonalizability assumption is needed in that spectrum formula.

By [def-wf-iota-real] and step 1, $\iota P_x(\mathcal G_0,T)=\prod_{i=1}^s(1-\lambda_iT)$ has real coefficients, so complex conjugation of coefficients fixes it and $\prod_i(1-\overline{\lambda_i}T)=\prod_i(1-\lambda_iT)$. Since $f$ is invertible, every $\lambda_i\neq0$, and the $\lambda_i$ with multiplicity are the inverses of the roots of this polynomial; hence the multiset $\{\lambda_i\}$ is conjugation stable. Choose a permutation $\sigma$ of the indexed occurrences with $\overline{\lambda_i}=\lambda_{\sigma(i)}$. The map $I\mapsto\sigma(I)$ bijects the $r$-element subsets. For each $I$, $\overline{\prod_{i\in I}\lambda_i}=\prod_{i\in I}\overline{\lambda_i}=\prod_{j\in\sigma(I)}\lambda_j$. This bijection proves conjugation stability of $M_r$ including multiplicities; it does not require distinct eigenvalues. For $r=0$ there is one subset and its product is $1$.

source.place: third sentence: conjugation permutes the product multiset

proof.text: By step 1, the local characteristic factor of the exterior power in [def-wf-iota-real] is $P_{x,r}(T)=\det(1-T\bigwedge^rf\mid\bigwedge^rV)$, and after applying $\iota$ step 2 gives $\iota P_{x,r}(T)=\prod_{\mu\in M_r}(1-\mu T)$. Conjugating its coefficients gives $\prod_{\mu\in M_r}(1-\overline\mu T)=\iota P_{x,r}(T)$, since the preceding step permutes the factors with multiplicity. Hence every coefficient is real. This holds at every closed point $x$, so the exterior power is $\iota$-real by the same definition. When $r=s$ the same calculation has the single product of all eigenvalues; if $s=0$, the allowed case $r=0$ has factor $1-T$.

source.place: last two sentences: real local factors and the pointwise conclusion

proof_origin.place: entire proof, expanded at the fibre comparison and indexed-subset permutation
